subject: DPA negotiation: geo-conditional purge, notification window & tombstone manifest
messages:
From: Sofia Delgado <sofia.delgado@npv-solutions.com>
To: avery_johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: legal@npv-solutions.com, CISO Team <ciso@npv-solutions.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA negotiation: geo-conditional purge, notification window & tombstone manifest

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're moving through our procurement/infosec review and have three items we want explicit language for in the DPA before we can sign:

1) Deletion notification window — we need a guaranteed 48-hour advance notice to coordinate our legal hold processes (instead of the current 7-day notice).
2) Geofence (regional) purge behavior — when a customer requests onshore-only deletion, we need a clear sequence for staged removal (primary, replica, snapshots) and an acknowledgement token ('tombstone manifest') that proves each step completed.
3) Tombstone certification — we ask for a vendor-signed manifest or technical receipt that we can store with audit artifacts.

I've attached a redline (NPV_DPA_Redline_v3.docx) with suggested clauses. Can you confirm which items Redwood can commit to verbatim, where you need alternative language, and any required operational lead time? Also: if you support a 48-hour notification, is that calendar or business days?

Appreciate a short runbook/ops description too — our security team needs to map it to internal playbooks.

Best,
Sofia Delgado
Head of Procurement
NPV Solutions

Attachments: NPV_DPA_Redline_v3.docx

From: avery_johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sofia Delgado <sofia.delgado@npv-solutions.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA negotiation: geo-conditional purge, notification window & tombstone manifest

Sofia — thanks for the redline and clear asks. Looping in Marissa (Legal) and Laura (Ops) so we can respond with precise language and operational constraints. Quick answers up front:

- 48-hour notice: operationally we can accommodate a 48-hour notification "as a target" but need to clarify calendar vs. business days and whether an expedited path exists for court orders/legal holds.
- Tombstone manifest: we can provide a cryptographic receipt-style acknowledgment for replica deletion and snapshot tombstoning, but the exact form of the artifact will need to be scoped (JSON manifest vs. signed PDF).
- Staged removal sequencing: we can commit to a staged workflow (primary -> replicas -> snapshots -> backup epochs) with SLO windows for each stage; the SLOs depend on the retention tier (hot/warm/cold).

Marissa — can you review the attached redline and propose precise clause language we can offer as alternatives? Laura — can you draft a 1-page ops runbook that explains: trigger event, proof artifact, estimated SLOs per storage tier, and rollback/hold procedure?

Sofia — could you confirm whether NPV requires the 48-hour notice to be business days, and whether the tombstone manifest needs to be human-signed or machine-verifiable?

Thanks,
Avery Johnson

On Tue, Aug 10, 2027 at 09:38 AM Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.inference.com> wrote:
> Sofia — thanks for the redline and clear asks. Looping in Marissa (Legal) and Laura (Ops) so we can respond with precise language and operational constraints. Quick answers up front:
>
> - 48-hour notice: operationally we can accommodate a 48-hour notification "as a target" but need to clarify calendar vs. business days and whether an expedited path exists for court orders/legal holds.
> - Tombstone manifest: we can provide a cryptographic receipt-style acknowledgment for replica deletion and snapshot tombstoning, but the exact form of the artifact will need to be scoped (JSON manifest vs. signed PDF).
> - Staged removal sequencing: we can commit to a staged workflow (primary -> replicas -> snapshots -> backup epochs) with SLO windows for each stage; the SLOs depend on the retention tier (hot/warm/cold).

Thanks for that clarity. To confirm NPV's stance:

- 48-hour notice = business days (we have cross-border on-call rotations and legal review that don't run on weekends).
- Tombstone manifest must be machine-verifiable with a cryptographic signature we can ingest into our evidence store (prefer JSON + SHA256 + signature).
- For staged removal we expect the vendor to provide:
  * a manifest per deletion request listing object IDs + storage tiers,
  * timestamps for each stage,
  * an overall completion flag once all stages are finished.

I've uploaded an updated redline that adds this language to section 4 (see attachment). Two follow-ups:

1) If Redwood cannot meet machine-verifiable manifests for warm/cold snapshot purges (due to dedupe/compaction), would a signed operational certificate summarizing the purge window and sample hashes be acceptable?
2) What is Redwood's operational SLA for completing the full staged removal for hot vs. cold tiers (ballpark in hours/days)?

Appreciate the quick turn here — our security team wants to finalize this during the week.

Regards,
Sofia Delgado
Head of Procurement
NPV Solutions

Attachments: NPV_DPA_Redline_v3.docx, tombstone-cert-spec.pdf

Subject: Re: DPA negotiation: geo-conditional purge, notification window & tombstone manifest

Sofia — thanks for the updated redline and the clear machine-verifiable requirement. Quick refresh from Legal + Ops after internal review:

1) Notification window: we can accept 48 business hours (not calendar days) for scheduled purges. For court orders or lawful process, we will prioritize expedited execution and will notify within 4 business hours of receipt. We'll propose clause language: "Vendor shall provide Customer with no less than forty-eight (48) business hours' prior notice for scheduled deletion requests absent an emergency lawful process."

2) Tombstone manifest / proof artifact: Redwood can provide a JSON manifest signed with Redwood's key containing: request_id, object_ids (or object id ranges), storage_tier flags, stage timestamps, and SHA256 sample hashes. For warm/cold tiers where per-object hashes are impractical due to dedup/compaction, we will provide a signed operational certificate that includes: time window, replica sets affected, start/end timestamps, and a sample of N hashes of affected files along with a link to immutable audit logs. Suggested clause alternative: "Vendor shall provide machine-verifiable deletion artifacts. Where per-object cryptographic verification is not technically feasible, Vendor may provide a vendor-signed operational certificate and immutable audit log reference."

3) SLOs (ballpark):
  - Hot tier (active replicas in-region): completion target within 24 hours after the 48-hour notice window.
  - Warm tier (nearline replicas/snapshots): completion target within 7 calendar days after notice window.
  - Cold tier (archival backups): completion target within 30 calendar days with documented handoff for escrowed backups.

4) Evidence delivery: manifests/certificates will be delivered as a downloadable artifact (signed JSON or signed PDF) with SHA256 checksum and retained in our audit log for 12 months by default; longer retention can be negotiated.

Next steps we propose:
- Laura will post an ops runbook (internal) and a sanitized public runbook for customers by EOD tomorrow.
- I will draft conservative clause text to replace the NPV redline; we can then do a short call to agree wording.

If that approach works, can we schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk through the proposed clause text and the runbook? Avery — please share Laura's runbook link when available (internal link OK).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
